key_insight: LLMSurgeon shows that you can infer a large language model’s pretraining data mixture from its generated text alone, effectively treating the model’s corpus composition as a diagnosable "digital DNA." This enables post-hoc auditing of where a model likely learned from, even when training data is undisclosed.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of transparency around LLM pretraining data mixtures, which makes it difficult to audit provenance, detect bias sources, or understand why a model behaves the way it does.
method: Defines Data Mixture Surgery (DMS): estimate the domain-level distribution of an LLM’s pretraining corpus using only model-generated text.
Uses a predefined domain taxonomy to map outputs back to likely training-data composition.
Introduces LLMSurgeon as the diagnostic framework for recovering and analyzing the data mixture of target LLMs.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical auditing tool to better understand model behavior, improve accountability, and investigate bias or failure modes tied to training data composition. It can also support model comparison, provenance analysis, and safer deployment decisions.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: generated text -> domain classifier -> estimated data mixture distribution
Stacked bar chart comparing inferred pretraining mixtures across models
Taxonomy wheel or domain map showing the predefined corpus categories
Diagnostic analogy graphic linking LLM outputs to "digital DNA" or medical surgery imagery
paper_title: LLMSurgeon: Diagnosing Data Mixture of Large Language Models
paper_authors: Yaxin Luo, Jiacheng Cui, Xiaohan Zhao, Xinyi Shang, Jiacheng Liu
